clue.text: Old table put behind trophy cabinet

indicators.note: the table goes after the trophy, so it sits behind it in the answer

parts.note: a trophy is often a cup
a board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone shoves an antique table behind the trophy cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a storage cabinet with shelves and doors.

clue.text: Broadcast scene from Monday play?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A scene from a Monday drama goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the answer is a kind of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy of manners is a genre of stage play satirising social behaviour.

clue.text: Expert setter upset after introduction

parts.note: an expert is a pro

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so me

explanation.surface: A professional compiler gets annoyed after an opening remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is the compiler speaking of himself, so ME, which 'upset' turns to EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or preamble to a book or speech.

clue.text: "Spectator" and one of our rivals?

explanation.definitionFit: An observer is an onlooker; The Observer is a Sunday newspaper competing with this paper, The Sunday Times.

clue.text: Polish right for small flower

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: to polish is to shine

explanation.surface: A gardener polishes a little flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows: a river. Here it is the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, so crossword setters call it a flower; the Rhine is a European river.

clue.text: Epic novel about a Conservative that could make you puke

indicators.note: novel means new, so the word epic is given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A long political novel about a Tory that is enough to make a reader sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a link here, not a container signal. Ipecac is a plant extract once used to make people vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a root extract formerly given as an emetic to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Chessman takes rook to force way through

indicators.note: takes means the piece holds the rook letter inside it

parts.note: a chessman is a piece
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: In chess, one man captures a rook to break through the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to penetrate, making a hole through something.

clue.text: Made short dog follow journalist

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to tail someone is to follow them
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A dog is set to trail a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailed means cut short or reduced.

clue.text: City has corporals doing wicked stuff at the front

indicators.note: wicked suggests going astray, so the letters of corporals doing are twisted
at the front picks the opening letter of stuff

explanation.surface: Soldiers get up to mischief in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges CORPORALS DOING; the first letter of 'stuff' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a city in the US state of Colorado.

clue.text: Sells ham to be cooked where soldiers eat

indicators.note: cooked means altered or fiddled, so the letters of sells ham are mixed up

explanation.surface: A shop sells ham for cooking in an army canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess hall is the dining room in a military base.

clue.text: Male visits sleazy Soho inn at start of evening for dodgy booze

indicators.note: sleazy suggests something corrupt and disordered, so the letters of Soho inn are jumbled
at start of points to just the opening letter of evening

explanation.surface: A man drops into a seedy Soho pub one evening for some suspect liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visits' only joins the male letter to the rest. Soho is a London district known for its nightlife and seedy reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled spirit, liquor made and sold outside the law.

clue.text: Some bachelor never returned record

indicators.note: returned means that run of letters is read backwards
some of the words bachelor never supplies a short run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A bachelor never gave back a borrowed record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks LORNE out of bachelOR NEver, and 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To record is to enter a name on a register, as one does when signing up.

clue.text: This object can be reserved if seen before end of sale

indicators.note: the answer placed in front of the last letter of sale spells the word for reserved, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: reserved means modest and quiet, demure

indicators.note: end of sale is the final letter of the word sale

explanation.surface: A notice says this item can be put aside if spotted before the sale closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'This ... can be reserved if seen before end of sale' as: this word plus E (sale's last letter) makes DEMURE, reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Relaxed boss of meeting — in such?

definitions.text: Relaxed boss of meeting — in such?

parts.note: relaxed means easy-going
the person presiding over a meeting is the chair

explanation.surface: A laid-back person running a meeting, lounging in the right sort of seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a relaxed meeting boss would sit in one.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable armchair for lounging in.

clue.text: Being exhausted and vague is overcome by superior tactics

parts.note: exhausted means used up, out
vague means broad, general rather than specific

explanation.surface: Someone tired and woolly-minded gets beaten by cleverer manoeuvring.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgeneral an opponent is to beat them through better generalship and strategy.

clue.text: Lecture singer about Elvis after end of concert

indicators.note: after means the rest of the wordplay follows that final letter
end of picks the final letter of concert
about means the singer goes round the word for Elvis

parts.note: an alto is a singer
Elvis Presley is nicknamed the King

explanation.surface: A singer gives an Elvis talk at the end of a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding, a telling-off.

clue.text: Prisoner on cycle seen going off about to hide

indicators.note: about means the rearranged seen surrounds the other letters
going off means the letters of seen go astray
on in a down clue means the prisoner sits above the cycle letter

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
C is an abbreviation for cycle

explanation.surface: A convict on a bike is spotted fleeing, about to go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to hide' but works as the container signal; 'on' stacks the prisoner above the cycle letter in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce is to settle somewhere snug and safe, tucked away out of sight.

clue.text: Lump left in fish

indicators.note: in means the letter for left is placed inside the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone finds a lump left inside a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a lump of earth or clay.

clue.text: During latter part of play audience finally becomes still

parts.note: during means in
Act IV is a late section of a play

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of audience

explanation.surface: Late in the play, the audience at last falls silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means motionless and doing nothing.

clue.text: Island lacks a strong drink

indicators.note: lacks a means the island name loses one letter a

parts.note: Malta is a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: An island is said to be short of hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is short for malt whisky, a spirit.

clue.text: Walks east on short narrow road wearing suit

indicators.note: wearing means the suit is put on around the shortened road

parts.note: spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: short means the road word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A man in a suit strolls along a narrow road heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is a card suit; 'wearing' then reads naturally as one word put around another.
explanation.definitionFit: Esplanades are seafront promenades where people stroll, so walks.

clue.text: Accuse cleaner, say, on return

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady

indicators.note: on return means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: EG is short for for example, say

explanation.surface: A cleaner is accused when someone comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (charwoman) is a British cleaner; 'on return' turns EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to accuse formally of an offence.

clue.text: The chancellor's position relative to number 10?

definitions.text: The chancellor's position relative to number 10?

parts.words: The chancellor's position relative to number 10?
parts.note: the Chancellor of the Exchequer lives at 11 Downing Street, right next door to the Prime Minister at Number 10

explanation.surface: A question about how the Chancellor ranks against the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' suggests rank or political standing; it is literally where the house stands. The UK Chancellor's official home is beside Number 10, the Prime Minister's.
explanation.definitionFit: Living next door to someone makes you the person beside them on the street.

clue.text: Be effective in controlling poise during dance

indicators.note: during means the poise letter is placed within the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively dance
P is the symbol for the poise, a unit of viscosity

explanation.surface: A dancer keeps their balance well during a reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poise' is not balance but a unit of viscosity, symbol P.
explanation.definitionFit: A repellent works by keeping pests away, holding them in check.

clue.text: Person in tent disposes of medium skip

indicators.note: disposes of means the letter for medium is thrown out

parts.note: someone sleeping in a tent is a camper
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A camper throws away a medium-sized item.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful leap or skip.

clue.text: In gym man is lying face downwards

indicators.note: in means the man is placed inside the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym lessons
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: In the gym a man lies flat on his front.
explanation.definitionFit: Prone means lying flat with the front of the body facing down.

clue.text: Scorer left gear outside when changing

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged gear goes round the letter for left
changing means the letters of gear are altered in order

explanation.surface: A footballer leaves his kit outside the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when changing' turns GEAR into EGAR, and 'outside' wraps it round L. A 'scorer' here writes musical scores: Edward Elgar, the English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar was a composer, someone who writes musical scores.

clue.text: Goat with maize on island

indicators.note: on means the maize word comes after the island

parts.note: Capri is an Italian island
maize is called corn in many places

explanation.surface: A goat eating maize on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is the zodiac sign whose symbol is a goat.

clue.text: Tool seen in old shed behind school

indicators.note: behind means the shed comes after the school letter

parts.note: a hovel is a wretched hut or open shed

explanation.surface: A tool turns up in a tumbledown shed behind the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a digging implement.

clue.text: Having no idea how this puzzle started!

explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means ignorant, and before a setter writes them a crossword grid is without any clues.
